title: Interactive Clinical Data Explorer
text:
Below is an interactive clinical data explorer running directly in your browser via WebAssembly (Shinylive):
#| '!! shinylive warning !!': |
#|   shinylive does not work in self-contained HTML documents.
#|   Please set `embed-resources: false` in your metadata.
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 650
#| viewerWidth: 100%

library(shiny)

# 1. UI Definition
ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(bootswatch = "flatly"),
  titlePanel("CDISC ADSL Variable Explorer"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("variable", "Select Demographic Metric:", 
                  choices = c("Age" = "AGE", "Baseline Height (cm)" = "HEIGHT", "Baseline Weight (kg)" = "WEIGHT")),
      sliderInput("bins", "Histogram Bins:", min = 5, max = 25, value = 12),
      checkboxInput("show_table", "Show Raw Data Table", value = TRUE)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("distPlot"),
      hr(),
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = "input.show_table == true",
        tableOutput("dataTable")
      )
    )
  )
)

# 2. Server Definition
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Synthetic ADSL Patient Data
  set.seed(42)
  adsl <- data.frame(
    USUBJID = paste0("PAT-", 101:120),
    AGE = round(rnorm(20, mean = 58, sd = 8)),
    HEIGHT = round(rnorm(20, mean = 168, sd = 10), 1),
    WEIGHT = round(rnorm(20, mean = 74, sd = 12), 1)
  )

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    val <- adsl[[input$variable]]
    hist(val, breaks = input$bins, col = "#2c3e50", border = "white",
         xlab = input$variable, main = paste("Distribution of", input$variable))
  })

  output$dataTable <- renderTable({
    head(adsl[, c("USUBJID", input$variable)], 8)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Kaplan Meier Curve Data Preparation
text:
ADTTE column descriptions








Variable
Name
In this study




STUDYID
Study Identifier
Always CDISCPILOT01; identifies the trial


SITEID
Study Site Identifier
Which of the 17 clinical sites enrolled the patient (701–718)


USUBJID
Unique Subject Identifier
The patient key (e.g., 01-701-1015) that links ADTTE to every other dataset; 254 patients, one row each


AGE
Age
Age in years at baseline (51–89)


AGEGR1
Pooled Age Group 1
Age category: <65, 65-80, >80


AGEGR1N
Pooled Age Group 1 (N)
Numeric code for AGEGR1 (1, 2, 3), used for sorting


RACE
Race
WHITE, BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN, AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE


RACEN
Race (N)
Numeric code for RACE, used for sorting


SEX
Sex
F or M


TRTSDT
Date of First Exposure to Treatment
First dose date; copied from ADSL


TRTEDT
Date of Last Exposure to Treatment
Last dose date; copied from ADSL


TRTDUR
Duration of Treatment (days)
Days on treatment, from TRTSDT to TRTEDT (1–212)


TRTP
Planned Treatment
The arm the patient was assigned to


TRTA
Actual Treatment
The arm the patient actually received; the grouping variable for the KM curves


TRTAN
Actual Treatment (N)
Numeric code for TRTA: 0 = Placebo, 54 = Low Dose, 81 = High Dose (the daily dose in mg)


PARAM
Parameter Description
Time to First Dermatologic Event; the full name of the endpoint


PARAMCD
Parameter Code
TTDE, so we filter to the endpoint we want


AVAL
Analysis Value
Number of days from STARTDT to ADT, counting the start day as Day 1; the x-axis of the KM curve


STARTDT
Time-to-Event Origin Date
Day 1 of the clock; here it’s the first dose date (TRTSDT)


ADT
Analysis Date
The date the clock stopped, either the event date or the censoring date


CNSR
Censor
0 = had a dermatologic event, 1 = censored


EVNTDESC
Event or Censoring Description
Why the clock stopped: Dematologic Event Occured (typo is in the original data) or Study Completion Date


SRCDOM
Source Domain
Which dataset ADT came from: ADAE for events, ADSL for censored patients


SRCVAR
Source Variable
Which column ADT came from: ASTDT (AE start date) or RFENDT (end-of-study date)


SRCSEQ
Source Sequence Number
Which row in ADAE the event came from (matches AESEQ); blank for censored patients


SAFFL
Safety Population Flag
Y = received at least one dose; all 254 patients are in the safety population
